idiom_name: undefined with optional chaining (?.) and nullish coalescing (??)
implementation_notes: JavaScript encodes absence in undefined (never assigned) and null (deliberate empty), and modern syntax makes reads through absence safe: the optional chaining operator ?. short-circuits to undefined instead of throwing when the receiver is null or undefined, and ?? supplies a default only for those two values, unlike || which also fires for 0 and ''. Nothing in the language forces a caller to handle absence - there are no signatures - so the realization degrades to a discipline: keep undefined as the single empty value, never overload null/0/''/false as absence, and let JSDoc or TypeScript carry the contract. The classic Maybe wrapper is replaced by undefined plus the two operators; a Maybe library (fp-ts, Sanctuary) is justified only in a code base that already works in a functional pipeline style.
pitfalls: undefined and null are two absence values that are both falsy along with 0, '' and NaN: a single !value test collapses them, so compare explicitly.
delete obj.k removes the property while obj.k = undefined keeps the key present; Object.keys, JSON.stringify and `in` treat the two differently.
Optional chaining short-circuits only the chain it is written on: after a grouping or a further dot the next access still throws on the absent value.
Array holes, missing Map entries and out-of-range indices all read as undefined, so 'not found' and 'stored undefined' are indistinguishable without an explicit has/in check.
